note: Our statements of standard biology consistent with the syllabus. Each sense needs two-source verification before any card that relies on it is published.

terms.sense: The region where the two sister chromatids of a replicated chromosome are held together.
The organelle, a pair of centrioles in animal cells, that organises the spindle.
DNA with histone proteins, loosely coiled, in a nucleus that is not dividing.
Condensed DNA with histone proteins; after replication it consists of two sister chromatids joined at the centromere.
A cap of repeated DNA sequence at each end of a chromatid; part of it is lost at each replication, protecting the genes behind it.
terms.homonym_warning: A metaphase chromosome has two chromatids and so four telomeres.

terms.sense: A sequence of nucleotides, part of a DNA molecule, that codes for a polypeptide.
Three bases on mRNA that code for one amino acid or a stop signal.
Three bases on a tRNA molecule, complementary to a codon on mRNA.
Making mRNA from the template strand of a gene, using RNA nucleotides.
Making a polypeptide at a ribosome, in the order of the codons on mRNA.
The transport of assimilates such as sucrose and amino acids in the phloem.
Each new DNA molecule holds one whole original strand and one newly made strand.
terms.homonym_warning: Describes molecules, not halves of strands.

terms.sense: How many times larger the image is than the real object.
The smallest distance at which two points can still be seen as separate; a property of the microscope.
The place where an organism lives.
The role of an organism: the conditions it tolerates, the resources it uses and its interactions with other organisms.
A line along which samples are taken, positioned deliberately to show change across a gradient.
A frame that marks out a known area for sampling.
The attraction between water molecules, caused by hydrogen bonds.
The attraction between water molecules and other surfaces such as cell walls.
The cell walls and spaces between cells, through which water can move.
The cytoplasm of cells joined by plasmodesmata, through which water can move.
The permanent loss of the three-dimensional shape of a protein, and so of its function, by extremes of temperature or pH.
terms.homonym_warning: A small change near the optimum is reversible and is not denaturation.

terms.sense: A molecule on the surface of a cell or pathogen that triggers an immune response.
terms.homonym_warning: Self antigens are on the body's own cells; non-self antigens are not.

terms.sense: A protein made by plasma cells that binds one specific antigen.
terms.homonym_warning: An antibody is a molecule, not a cell.

terms.sense: Small projections of the cell surface membrane that increase surface area for absorption.
Longer projections of the cell surface membrane that beat to move material along.
How close a result is to the true value.
Whether repeating the work gives consistent results.
The variable the investigator changes.
The variable that is measured.
